findings.title: Add handler indexes e.Fields[0] without guarding
findings.message: The Change handler is invoked directly by the editor and the gallery's Change callback dereferences m.rules, which is fine, but Validate for a group requires Value to be exactly zero while a Rule with Group and nil Rules is allowed; more importantly, the text rule value check rejects any Number/Checked, yet changing a boolean field operator or value from an empty-leaf group is fine. The real issue: the 4096 limit counts bytes but an empty group (no children) is valid, so a root with zero rules is acceptable while the default add path assumes e.Fields[0] exists without re-validation under concurrent mutation.
findings.suggestion: Ensure edits re-validate Fields before indexing e.Fields[0] in the add handler.

findings.title: Edit guard compares fields shallowly
findings.message: The gallery Change callback references m.rules.Root and mutates it; if the editor is replaced the stale closure still points at the new editor. Additionally, RuleEditor.View captures e by pointer, so copying the struct (check := *e) copies nextID and other state, fine, but callers who copy RuleEditor lose retention semantics silently.
findings.suggestion: Document that RuleEditor must not be copied, and add a copy guard.

findings.title: ID counter consumed by rejected proposals
findings.message: freshRuleID mutates e.nextID inside the edit callback even when the proposal is later rejected by the host. This is documented, but nextID is also consumed when the edit is a no-op in later validation, and the loop can burn up to 65 IDs per click. Also the check against the candidate only, not against previously proposed IDs, relies on the counter alone.
findings.suggestion: Only advance nextID after the candidate passes validation, or accept the documented behavior and cap retries.
